text:
The story around Cale Makar this week isn't his 21 points. It's his health. Denver Gazette reporter Evan Rawal posted on Nov. 8 that Makar "just exited practice with the trainer and seemed to be pointing to a lower body issue," and the Avalanche recalled defenseman Alex Gagne the next day. That came a week after a hit from Chicago's Artyom Levshunov that Rawal called questionable.

Until then he was doing Makar things. Five goals and 16 assists in 17 games, 8 on the power play, and a 58.1% share of 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 8.5 points above the Avs without him. He's shooting 10.9%, a little above his usual range, so the goals may slow; the passing won't. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 97th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists last season.

Two Norris Trophies, a Conn Smythe and a Cup say what Colorado stands to lose if this lingers. Watch the injury report before anything else.
headline: The Avalanche hold their breath on Makar
